content: Projects on slopes above fifteen percent require a geotechnical slope stability report before structural plan approval.
Retaining walls above the local height threshold require engineered calculations, drainage details, and a separate structural permit.
Grading or construction near mapped wetlands requires a delineation survey and environmental buffer review before earthwork begins.
Development in a floodplain must document base flood elevation, finished floor elevation, and flood resistant construction measures.
Disturbed soil areas require silt fencing, stabilized entrances, sediment controls, and inspection after major rainfall.
Large impervious areas require stormwater detention calculations, controlled discharge, and an operations maintenance plan.
Emergency vehicle access must meet minimum clear width, turning radius, grade, and all weather surface requirements.
Public entrances require an accessible route with compliant ramp slope, landings, handrails, and maneuvering clearance.
Exterior work in a designated historic district requires preservation review for materials, massing, windows, and visible alterations.
Demolition applications require an asbestos survey, utility disconnect confirmations, waste handling details, and site protection measures.
Deep excavation beside adjacent foundations requires a shoring design, underpinning assessment, and construction monitoring plan.
Construction noise is restricted to approved working hours, with additional limits for weekends and residential areas.
